currentContext.strengths: Asset-light managed-aggregation (MA) sourcing model in which developers bear all or part of fit-out cost against a minimum guarantee plus revenue/profit share, reducing upfront capital intensity and occupancy risk while enabling rapid expansion; the Company intends to hold roughly a 60:40 MA-to-straight-lease mix|Pan-India scale and network density - around 250 operational centres across 18 cities and leading micro-markets within them, a scale advantage the MD&A notes favours 'scaled, well-capitalised operators with pan-India networks and design-and-build capability'|End-to-end integrated platform across coworking, managed offices, design-and-build (Transform by Awfis) and furniture/fit-out (Frame by Awfis), enabling cross-sell and ancillary revenue per seat|Enterprise/MNC quality of the client base at 64%, multi-centre clients at about 48% and weighted-average client tenure of about 37 months with roughly 26-month lock-ins - a source of revenue visibility and switching cost|GCC franchise: 100+ GCC clients across 9 cities contributing about 23% of rental revenue, with 14 major GCC mandates closed during FY26|Premiumisation of supply - 100% of new centres signed in Grade A/A+ assets and 35 premium Gold/Elite centres, supporting realisations and client quality|Multi-channel distribution - Awfis mobile app, an extensive network of domestic and international property consultants and third-party aggregator platforms, plus an in-house sales team and community managers|Balance-sheet strength: credit rating upgraded to A+ (Stable) and a net-cash position maintained throughout FY26|Technology stack - AI-based development framework, AI-driven data democracy, SD-WAN hub architecture for faster site deployment, and IT management tooling (ManageEngine, SolarWinds)
currentContext.strategies: Consolidate leadership in Indian flexible workspace by leveraging the asset-light managed-aggregation model, premium services and an ecosystem spanning advanced workspace design and comprehensive support solutions|Methodically expand the pan-India presence while elevating the client-centric value proposition, to capture escalating demand for flexible workspace|Expand presence in Tier-II cities and high-potential micro-markets, supported by growing demand for flexible work models among large corporates and MNCs|Sharpen focus on occupancy optimisation and high-margin allied offerings within the enterprise and managed-office business|Broaden the allied-services portfolio - Awfis Cafe, TechLabs for IT and network solutions, premium sustainable employee-transportation partnerships, event management, mobility and concierge - to deliver turnkey workplace solutions and generate ancillary revenue per seat|Operate a two-segment portfolio - Space Solutions (coworking, enterprise/managed offices, allied services) and Transform by Awfis (design, construction and fit-out) - while scaling Frame by Awfis, a capital-light furniture and fit-out offering launched during the year|Serve GCC and multinational demand through customised enterprise workspace solutions, including dedicated and partial-managed configurations|Continue technology absorption - further integration of AI and machine learning, a shift to cloud-based solutions, enhanced IoT management and continued emphasis on automation and orchestration, on top of an AI-based development framework, AI-driven data democracy and SD-WAN hub architecture that speeds new-site deployment|Pursue green building certifications such as LEED and reduce environmental footprint through energy-conservation, daylighting, energy-efficient equipment and recycling initiatives
currentContext.expansion: Awfis expanded its flexible-workspace footprint materially during FY26: the Directors' Report states that the Company added 41 new centres and 30K operational seats during the year, expanding its signed network to 266 centres with approximately 184K seats across 18 cities spanning Tier-1 and Tier-2 markets, serving a diversified client base of about 3.5K customers. The signed network figure includes centres still under fit-out and signed letters of intent, so it represents the forward opening pipeline rather than the operational base. Expansion is executed against an industry backdrop management describes as constructive - flex penetration trending toward roughly 25% of office leasing by 2027, GCC and enterprise mandates driving larger, longer-tenure deals, and Tier-II cities growing disproportionately fast from a smaller base - while management flags that interest rates, construction costs and commercial rentals influence the cost of capacity addition, and that availability and timing of Grade A/A+ supply in preferred micro-markets is a constraint on the pace of expansion. On the corporate-structure side, the Company incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, Awfis Transform Private Limited, on December 3, 2025, and the Board and shareholders approved the transfer of the Design and Build business to it on a slump-sale basis on November 11, 2025 and January 23, 2026 respectively. No rupee capex quantum is disclosed in this bundle: the capital-commitments note arrives with its label but no figure and no printed unit, and the block headed as segment capital expenditure contains only the macroeconomic paragraph about public capital expenditure, not a segment capex row. Separately, the Directors' Report states that capital investment on energy conservation equipment was Nil and expenditure on research and development was Nil.

risks.note: MD&A Risk Management states that rapid capacity addition can temporarily depress blended occupancy until centres mature - a structural drag when the network is growing fast. Mitigation cited: disciplined, demand-led site selection, forward leasing, and active renewal and churn management.

risks.risk: Client concentration and re-leasing risk on large dedicated centres
risks.note: Large, highly customised dedicated centres carry re-leasing and refurbishment risk at the end of lock-in periods, so a single enterprise exit can strand purpose-built capacity. Mitigation cited: a selective approach to very large back-to-back deals and a diversified, multi-centre client base.

risks.risk: Execution and project-timing risk in design-and-build
risks.note: Design-and-build revenue is exposed to project deferrals, execution delays and regulatory factors, making that revenue stream lumpier than the recurring workspace business. Mitigation cited: a stronger order book and a shift toward larger, higher-value mandates.

Rising lease liabilities and finance costs accompany network growth - the core financial consequence of adding centres. Managed, per the MD&A, through the capital-light managed-aggregation model, a net-cash balance sheet and a strong credit rating; the Opportunities and Challenges section separately flags that movements in interest rates, construction costs and commercial rentals influence the cost of capacity addition.

Global energy prices, the West Asia conflict, trade-policy and visa developments could affect occupier sentiment and the pace of MNC and GCC expansion decisions; changes in taxation, real-estate regulation, GST treatment and workplace norms could affect the operating environment. The MD&A argues the diversified client and city mix provides resilience. Availability and timing of Grade A/A+ supply in preferred micro-markets is flagged as a separate constraint.

Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a material risk: increasing digitalisation, evolving regulatory requirements and rising cyber threats create exposure to data breaches, operational disruption, financial loss, regulatory penalties and reputational damage. Mitigation cited: information security policies, access controls and monitoring, periodic security audits, vulnerability assessments, penetration testing and employee awareness programmes, plus monitoring of data-protection compliance (the secretarial audit lists the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the IT Act among applicable laws).

risks.risk: Corporate governance, integrity and compliance risk
risks.note: BRSR material-issues table flags that inadequate governance, ethical misconduct or non-compliance with the Code of Conduct may result in regulatory action, financial loss, reputational damage and erosion of stakeholder trust. Mitigation cited: reinforced Code of Conduct compliance through communication, monitoring and periodic reviews, awareness and training programmes, and internal controls and oversight mechanisms; the Board has constituted a Risk Management Committee and states that, based on the assessment carried out during the year, there are no material risks which may threaten the existence of the Company.

risks.risk: Health, safety and workplace well-being affecting workforce availability and service delivery
risks.note: BRSR material-issues table notes that health and safety incidents, communicable diseases and adverse workplace conditions may affect employee well-being, workforce availability, productivity, service delivery and business continuity - material for a business whose product is the physical workplace itself. Mitigation cited: established health and safety practices, workplace hygiene, employee wellness initiatives, preventive measures, contingency planning and coordination with facility teams on ventilation and healthy workplace conditions.

one-line thesis: Awfis delivered robust 20% revenue growth and 30% EBITDA growth in Q3FY26 driven by mature center efficiency and GCC traction, though Transform segment faced temporary GRAP-related delays. Management prioritizes occupancy optimization over aggressive seat addition, guiding for 32k seats in FY26 with strong visibility on margin expansion as new centers mature.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs.382cr (+20% YoY); EBITDA: Rs.139cr (+30% YoY), Margin 36.5% (+270bps YoY); PAT (ex-exceptional): Rs.22cr (+47% YoY); Normalized EBITDA (IndAS adj): Rs.55cr (+18% YoY); Order Book: 11k seats (LOI) + 8L sqft MA pipeline; Net Debt: Negative (Net Cash Rs.96cr). One-offs: Transform revenue dip due to GRAP-IV pollution norms in North India.
guidance: Revenue Growth: ~30% (Co-working on track, Transform lagging); Margin: Expansion expected as new centers ramp; Order Inflow: Strong GCC pipeline (11 deals closed 9M, 11 going live H1FY27); Capex: Rs.200-210cr for FY26 (skewed to straight lease/elite).
order book & pipeline: 11 new centers (LOI) adding ~11k seats; 8L sqft Managed Aggregation pipeline (4.1L confirmed); Transform pipeline ~13L sqft (9L third-party + 4L managed aggregation).
segment / subsidiary detail: Co-working & Allied: Rs.322cr (+32% YoY), 84% of revenue; Awfis Transform: Rs.60cr (decline YoY due to execution delays); Occupancy: 75% blended (Mature >12mo: 84%); Client Mix: 64% Large Corp/MNC, 21% revenue from 80+ GCCs.
growth verticals / optionality: Tier-2 expansion (16% capacity growth); Gold/Elite format upmix; GCC first-mover advantage (20-30 new GCCs/quarter in India); Transform recovery post-GRAP normalization.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin 36.5% (Operating); Normalized margin impacted by IndAS 116; Pricing escalation 5-7% for SMEs, 4-5% for large cohorts; Depreciation rising due Elite/Straight-lease mix.
capex / expansion: Rs.159cr (9M FY26); Full year guidance Rs.200-210cr; Higher capex intensity due to shift toward Straight Lease (Elite/GCC centers) vs Managed Aggregation in 9M.
capital allocation: Net cash position (Rs.96cr including FDs); No debt; Capex focused on high-ROCE Elite centers and GCC mandates; No M&A disclosed.
risks & watch-items: GRAP/Regulatory execution delays (Transform); Concentration in North India for fit-out; Ramp-up lag for new centers (9-12 months to 80% occupancy); Lease expiry churn in mature centers.
management quality / tone: Confident on structural GCC demand; Prudent on capacity addition (lowered seat guide to 32k from 40k to protect margins); Transparent on Transform headwinds; Focus on quality of growth over speed.
non-obvious takeaways: Shift in capex mix: Higher straight-lease capex in 9M skewed by Elite/GCC deals, delaying Managed Aggregation ramp to Q4/Q1; Furniture business remains contract-manufactured with zero capex despite prior speculation; 45% of portfolio is <100 seats, providing diversification but lower tenure vs large cohorts.

themes.title: Flexible workspace, PropTech & commercial real-estate services
themes.need: The GCC build-out and hybrid-work shift drive managed/flexible office demand, and Q1FY27 showed flex becoming the marginal buyer of Indian office space. SMARTWORKS grew revenue 44% to INR 546cr with normalized EBITDA INR 107cr (+74%) at a 19.6% margin, lifted GCC clients from 15% to 21% of revenue in a single quarter, and reported India's highest-ever quarterly leasing at 24.6 mn sq ft with 27% of it through flex, up from 19% a year ago. PropTech consolidation started in the same quarter: AURUM announced the acquisition of Housing.com (~24% of India's online-portal share, 58mn monthly visits) at ~1.5x revenue against listed comparables at 4.5-10x, with Housing currently burning ~INR 200cr a year and committed to break even in four to six quarters. AWFIS/EFCIL/INDIQUBE/DEVX/WEWORK add managed workspace; NIRLON on office REIT-proxy assets.
themes.driver: GCC seat-count additions and flex share of net leasing; AURUM's four-to-six-quarter Housing.com breakeven clock; enterprise managed-office wins.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Tier-2 expansion (16% capacity growth); Gold/Elite format upmix; GCC first-mover advantage (20-30 new GCCs/quarter in India); Transform recovery post-GRAP normalization.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India is expected to remain among the fastest-growing large economies, with growth anchored by domestic consumption, public and private capital formation, a maturing services sector and continued GCC expansion - a macro backdrop management calls constructive for the commercial real-estate and flexible-workspace industry
- Occupier demand for Indian office space is expected to remain healthy, underpinned by the structural expansion of GCCs, the continued build-out of technology and financial-services capacity, and India's cost and talent advantages
- Flexible workspace is expected to take an increasing proportion of overall leasing as occupiers prioritise agility and capital efficiency, with penetration continuing toward roughly 25% of leasing by 2027
- Flex growth is likely to be led by enterprises and GCCs signing larger, longer-tenure managed-office and dedicated-centre mandates - a mix shift toward stickier, higher-tenure revenue
- A continued shift toward Grade A/A+ and premium, sustainability-certified space, with Grade A and sustainability-certified assets expected to command a growing share of demand (premiumisation as a realisation lever)
- Consolidation in favour of scaled, well-capitalised operators with pan-India networks and design-and-build capability - management states these trends 'play directly to the Company's strengths'
- Tier-II cities are likely to see disproportionately faster growth from a smaller base, broadening the addressable market
- The underpenetrated mid-market GCC segment of roughly 25-200 seats is described as directly aligned with the Company's flexible, managed and enterprise offerings; India adds an estimated 20-30 first-time GCCs every quarter and GCCs account for more than 40% of commercial real-estate leasing
- Demand is broadening beyond technology into BFSI, consulting, manufacturing and professional services, and beyond the largest cities into Tier-II markets
- A landlord-favourable cycle - healthy demand, a moderating supply pipeline in prime micro-markets, firming rentals and falling Grade A vacancy - is a cost-side consideration for capacity addition
- Allied services and premium formats are stated margin levers, boosting client satisfaction and ancillary revenue per seat
- Watch items management flags: global energy prices, trade policy and West Asia geopolitics; interest-rate, construction-cost and rental cycles; availability and timing of Grade A/A+ supply in preferred micro-markets; and changes in taxation, real-estate regulation, GST treatment and workplace norms
- Signed network expanded to 266 centres with approximately 184K seats across 18 cities during the year - signed supply that includes centres under fit-out and signed LOIs, versus the operational base, representing the forward opening pipeline
- 41 new centres and 30K operational seats were added during the year, serving a diversified client base of about 3.5K customers

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin 36.5% (Operating); Normalized margin impacted by IndAS 116; Pricing escalation 5-7% for SMEs, 4-5% for large cohorts; Depreciation rising due Elite/Straight-lease mix.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Net cash position (Rs.96cr including FDs); No debt; Capex focused on high-ROCE Elite centers and GCC mandates; No M&A disclosed.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Awfis expanded its flexible-workspace footprint materially during FY26: the Directors' Report states that the Company added 41 new centres and 30K operational seats during the year, expanding its signed network to 266 centres with approximately 184K seats across 18 cities spanning Tier-1 and Tier-2 markets, serving a diversified client base of about 3.5K customers. The signed network figure includes centres still under fit-out and signed letters of intent, so it represents the forward opening pipeline rather than the operational base. Expansion is executed against an industry backdrop management describes as constructive - flex penetration trending toward roughly 25% of office leasing by 2027, GCC and enterprise mandates driving larger, longer-tenure deals, and Tier-II cities growing disproportionately fast from a smaller base - while management flags that interest rates, construction costs and commercial rentals influence the cost of capacity addition, and that availability and timing of Grade A/A+ supply in preferred micro-markets is a constraint on the pace of expansion. On the corporate-structure side, the Company incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, Awfis Transform Private Limited, on December 3, 2025, and the Board and shareholders approved the transfer of the Design and Build business to it on a slump-sale basis on November 11, 2025 and January 23, 2026 respectively. No rupee capex quantum is disclosed in this bundle: the capital-commitments note arrives with its label but no figure and no printed unit, and the block headed as segment capital expenditure contains only the macroeconomic paragraph about public capital expenditure, not a segment capex row. Separately, the Directors' Report states that capital investment on energy conservation equipment was Nil and expenditure on research and development was Nil.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on structural GCC demand; Prudent on capacity addition (lowered seat guide to 32k from 40k to protect margins); Transparent on Transform headwinds; Focus on quality of growth over speed.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Asset-light managed-aggregation (MA) sourcing model in which developers bear all or part of fit-out cost against a minimum guarantee plus revenue/profit share, reducing upfront capital intensity and occupancy risk while enabling rapid expansion; the Company intends to hold roughly a 60:40 MA-to-straight-lease mix
- Pan-India scale and network density - around 250 operational centres across 18 cities and leading micro-markets within them, a scale advantage the MD&A notes favours 'scaled, well-capitalised operators with pan-India networks and design-and-build capability'
- End-to-end integrated platform across coworking, managed offices, design-and-build (Transform by Awfis) and furniture/fit-out (Frame by Awfis), enabling cross-sell and ancillary revenue per seat
- Enterprise/MNC quality of the client base at 64%, multi-centre clients at about 48% and weighted-average client tenure of about 37 months with roughly 26-month lock-ins - a source of revenue visibility and switching cost
- GCC franchise: 100+ GCC clients across 9 cities contributing about 23% of rental revenue, with 14 major GCC mandates closed during FY26
- Premiumisation of supply - 100% of new centres signed in Grade A/A+ assets and 35 premium Gold/Elite centres, supporting realisations and client quality
- Multi-channel distribution - Awfis mobile app, an extensive network of domestic and international property consultants and third-party aggregator platforms, plus an in-house sales team and community managers
- Balance-sheet strength: credit rating upgraded to A+ (Stable) and a net-cash position maintained throughout FY26
- Technology stack - AI-based development framework, AI-driven data democracy, SD-WAN hub architecture for faster site deployment, and IT management tooling (ManageEngine, SolarWinds)

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: GRAP/Regulatory execution delays (Transform); Concentration in North India for fit-out; Ramp-up lag for new centers (9-12 months to 80% occupancy); Lease expiry churn in mature centers.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Shift in capex mix: Higher straight-lease capex in 9M skewed by Elite/GCC deals, delaying Managed Aggregation ramp to Q4/Q1; Furniture business remains contract-manufactured with zero capex despite prior speculation; 45% of portfolio is <100 seats, providing diversification but lower tenure vs large cohorts.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Consolidate leadership in Indian flexible workspace by leveraging the asset-light managed-aggregation model, premium services and an ecosystem spanning advanced workspace design and comprehensive support solutions
- Methodically expand the pan-India presence while elevating the client-centric value proposition, to capture escalating demand for flexible workspace
- Expand presence in Tier-II cities and high-potential micro-markets, supported by growing demand for flexible work models among large corporates and MNCs
- Sharpen focus on occupancy optimisation and high-margin allied offerings within the …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:

|---|---|---|---|---|

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Industry] India flex market framed as structural: 18.6 MSF flex space leasing in 2025 (8x growth from 2017), ~3.5x increase in flexible workspace stock since 2020, flex at 21% share of office leasing in CY26 rising to 25% by 2027, and 55% of domestic and global occupiers already including flex in their portfolio.
- [Industry] India office market context: record 82.6 MSF office leasing in 2025 (3rd consecutive record year), 58.9 MSF new Grade A supply completions in 2025, and 21.9 MSF Q1 CY26 gross leasing (+13% YoY).
- [Industry-GCC] India GCC ecosystem cited (Nasscom-Zinnov, Colliers) at 2,117 GCCs / 3,728 units FY26E (from 510 / 1,025 in FY21), USD 98.4 Bn total GCC revenue FY26E, 2.36 Mn installed GCC talent and >40% share of Indian CRE leasing.
- [Assurance] M S K A & Associates LLP issued an agreed-upon procedures report dated August 13, 2026 under SRS 4400 validating the Cash EBITDA conversion adjustments and the PBT/revenue/EBITDA reconciliation for the quarter ended June 30, 2026.
- [Client wins] Key wins in the quarter include a global IT & consulting major in Pune (~3.0 lakh sq ft), a renewable energy group in Delhi (~1.0 lakh sq ft), a global e-commerce major in Bangalore (~67,000 sq ft), a diversified conglomerate in Hyderabad (~64,300 sq ft) and a global customer experience major in Mumbai (~50,000 sq ft).
